intended_object: The generic n×n permanent polynomial over ℂ, i.e. perm_n = Σ_{σ∈S_n} ∏_i x_{i,σ(i)} in ℂ[x_{ij} : i,j ∈ [n]]. This comes from the docstring and from how the file uses it in a formula-size lower bound over ℂ.
explanation:
The body applies Mathlib's `Matrix.permanent` (Σ_σ ∏_i M i (σ i)) to the generic matrix `Matrix.mvPolynomialX (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ`, whose (i,j) entry is `X (i,j)`. The result is exactly Σ_σ ∏_i X(i,σ i) in `MvPolynomial (Fin n × Fin n) ℂ`. The library's own lemma `permanentPolynomial_eq_sum` confirms this expansion. In the degenerate case n = 0 the result is 1, which is the standard convention (the empty product, with S_0 having one element).

The construction would make sense over any commutative ring. However, the docstring explicitly names the complex numbers, and the whole file works over ℂ: rational formulas over ℂ, evaluation at complex points, and partial derivatives evaluated at all-ones to give nonzero complex counts. Mathlib has no named "permanent polynomial" declaration, and the definition is a one-line composition of Mathlib's general constructions. So it is the specific object the docstring describes, in the setting the development needs, and I judge it faithful rather than too narrow.
